clue.text: Food for picnic spread I chew visiting beach

indicators.note: the scrambled letters call in on the beach word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a beach is sands

indicators.note: spread out loosely, so the letters of I chew are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at the seaside munching their packed lunch on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a picnic spread of food, but it signals that I CHEW is rearranged (into WICHE); 'visiting' then puts it within the beach word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread-wrapped fillings are the classic packed food carried on a picnic.

clue.text: Show is cut, bringing in little money

indicators.note: the cut word takes the money letter inside itself

parts.note: to slash is to cut
p, a penny, is a small British coin

explanation.surface: A theatre production is being axed, though it still earns a little.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a splash is to make a show, a showy display or noisy publicity.

clue.text: Browse books dipping into 'The Flower of Africa'

indicators.note: the books plunge inside the river's name, as into water

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; Africa's great river is the Nile
B is an abbreviation for book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: Someone leafs through a volume of African botany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is read as 'flow-er', a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazing animals browse by nibbling, taking small bites of leaves and shoots.

clue.text: Queen's expression showing a tremendous awe? Not exactly

indicators.note: the letters are not in their exact order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal remark that conveys great awe, or not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not exactly' rearranges A TREMENDOUS AWE, whose letters spell the famous phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: This frosty remark is traditionally attributed to Queen Victoria, using the royal plural.

clue.text: Temporary manager to have another go at test in vehicle

indicators.note: the resit word sits inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

parts.words: to have another go at test
parts.note: to retake an exam is to sit it again

explanation.surface: An interim boss resits a driving test in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker manager is an interim appointment in football, holding the job until a permanent one is found.

clue.text: Kitchen utensil's taken first slice off apple

indicators.note: the opening letter at the front of the utensil word is sliced away

parts.note: a beater, as in an egg beater, is a kitchen utensil

explanation.surface: A cook trims the first slice from an apple with a kitchen tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has'; the first slice removed is the single opening letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Growers call a dessert apple, one for eating raw rather than cooking, an eater.

clue.text: Mischievous child's endless racket

indicators.note: the final letter of the child word is dropped, leaving it without an end

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous child; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster makes an unending din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like noise, but here it means a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a fraudulent scheme, the same as a con or swindle.

clue.text: Granny in desire for agreement

indicators.note: the grandmother word goes inside the desire word

parts.note: to covet is to desire
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Grandma wants an agreement drawn up.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding pact or contract.

clue.text: Outlaws and William finally make mistake with strong desire to capture maiden

indicators.note: take only the last letter of the name William

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

indicators.note: the longing word holds the maiden letter inside it

parts.note: a yen is a strong desire
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Bandits and a man called William go wrong while lusting after a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaws and William' evokes Robin Hood's band; 'with' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood's band of outlaws in Sherwood Forest are known by this name.

clue.text: Blaming childish art — ordinary, not advanced

indicators.note: the ordinary letter takes the place of the advanced letter, which is no longer there

parts.note: finger painting is a children's art activity
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: Accusing children's artwork of being plain and unsophisticated.
explanation.walkthrough: O and A are the old British exam grades: O level (Ordinary) and A level (Advanced).
explanation.definitionFit: Pointing the finger at someone is an idiom for accusing them, so this is assigning blame.

clue.text: Balance achieved by former party of the centre — right area

parts.note: the Liberals, abbreviated Lib, were the old British centrist party before merging into the Lib Dems

explanation.surface: A political achievement of compromise by an old centrist party.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign is represented by the scales, an instrument for weighing.

clue.text: Dog with tail docked in old-fashioned style I always must follow

indicators.note: the end letter is cut off the style word, as a dog's tail is docked

parts.note: retro means in an old-fashioned style
ever means always

explanation.surface: A docked-tail dog trimmed in a vintage manner, with someone insisting on following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must follow' simply places I and EVER after the shortened style word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gundog breed trained to fetch shot game, such as the golden or Labrador variety.

clue.text: Work out clues with books, having enough resources

parts.note: to solve a crossword is to work out its clues
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A puzzler with plenty of reference books is well equipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Being solvent means having assets enough to pay all debts.

clue.text: There's remarkable energy about Conservative when deputy leader's in charge

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the party letter
remarkable suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters of energy are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory deputy shows great vigour while standing in for the leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' makes REGENY from ENERGY, and 'about' wraps it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: A regency is the period when a regent rules in place of an absent or underage monarch.

clue.text: Chef in big country house may have one?

definitions.text: Chef in big country house may have one?

parts.note: a chef is a cook
a grange is a large country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: A cook in a stately home would naturally have a big stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: such a chef would use one.
explanation.definitionFit: A large kitchen stove with oven and hotplates is what a house cook would work at.

clue.text: Lost again uneasily longing for the old days

indicators.note: the letters sit uneasily, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lost once more feels a restless yearning for the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental yearning for a past period.

clue.text: After church a Yankee turned up and almost messed up priest's garment

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay is placed after the church abbreviation
in a down clue the letters read upwards, so they are reversed

parts.note: US, the United States, is a Yankee's country

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is left off

parts.note: to blow something, as in blew it, is to mess it up

explanation.surface: An American bungles a vestment after a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns US into SU; 'almost' cuts BLEW to BLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is the sleeveless outer vestment worn by a priest celebrating Mass.

clue.text: Hyped-up spells of cricket out of date

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
old means out of date

explanation.surface: Bowling spells in a cricket match get overpromoted and dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oversold has been promoted with exaggerated claims.

clue.text: Fancy a soft drink consumed by kid

indicators.note: the drink phrase is swallowed inside the teasing phrase

parts.note: to kid is to tease, as in have someone on
Crush is a brand of fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: A child gulps down a fizzy pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the verb, meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy someone is to feel a romantic infatuation for them.

clue.text: Go along with tight corset

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Accompanying someone in a tightly laced undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort is to accompany someone as a companion or guard.

clue.text: Craft shops stocking unknown fragrant plant

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the unknown letter in stock inside them
craft as cunning, so the letters are artfully rearranged

parts.note: Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Craft shops sell an unfamiliar aromatic herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like part of 'craft shops' but signals the anagram of SHOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is an aromatic herb of the mint family.

clue.text: Small support sustaining a composer

indicators.note: the support word holds up the letter inside it

parts.note: a truss is a supporting framework or bandage

explanation.surface: A small brace holds up a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Strauss and Richard Strauss were famous composers of waltzes and operas.

clue.text: Sharp pain

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to sting or hurt

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both clever or stylish, and a stinging hurt.

clue.text: Pardon little woman keeping home

indicators.note: the woman's name keeps the home word inside it

parts.note: Amy March is one of the sisters in the novel Little Women
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: Forgiving a small lady who has stayed at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little woman' points to Amy, from Louisa May Alcott's Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: An official general pardon for offenders, especially political ones.

clue.text: One's projected to make a return flight

definitions.text: One's projected to make a return flight

parts.words: One's projected to make a return flight
parts.note: a thrown curved stick that flies back to its thrower, read cryptically as an aircraft round trip

explanation.definitionFit: A curved throwing stick designed to fly back to the thrower after being launched.

clue.text: Actor seen in clubs

explanation.surface: A performer spotted at a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Irons is an Oscar-winning actor, and metal-headed golf clubs share the name.

clue.text: Turning in the water, bear's heading off

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, of the bear word comes off

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A swirl in the water as a bear sets off.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a small whirlpool or swirling current.

clue.text: Honestly, it's what shepherd seeks in Bible reading

indicators.note: read out, the phrase is heard rather than seen

parts.words: it's what shepherd seeks in Bible
parts.note: in the parable the shepherd seeks a stray sheep; a tup is a ram, so a stray tup

explanation.surface: Truthfully, the shepherd in scripture is looking for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The parable of the lost sheep: the shepherd hunts a stray, and a tup is a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight up is an informal idiom meaning honestly, no word of a lie.
